_README: Deployment presets for liveClassifierTorchROS.py. This file is COMMITTED TO GIT so a
deployment site picks up new models and operating points with a plain `git pull` --
no environment variables to set on-site.
The FIRST entry of "configurations" is the one used at startup. To switch, either
reorder the list (and commit) or pass the preset name as an argument:
ros2 run magician_vision_classifier liveClassifierTorchROS --config low_false_alarm
The model's .pth/.json are auto-downloaded on first run from
http://ammar.gr/magician/models/CameraV2Models/ (ModelDownload.ensure_model), the same
directory scripts/uploadModels.sh pushes to.
gate.threshold semantics depend on gate.mode. Under the default "defect_mass" it
thresholds 1 - P(clean) -- the total probability mass on ANY defect class -- NOT the
max softmax probability. A max_prob threshold of the same number means something
completely different. Thresholds are NOT portable between models: re-read them from
that model's <name>_threshold_curve.json.
Every number under "measured" is read from the named threshold-curve file, not
estimated. They come from the run's held-out split, which was ALSO used to select the
checkpoint, so treat the absolute values as slightly optimistic -- the ranking between
operating points is sound (see ISSUES.md M3).
runtime.step / runtime.target_fps ARE tuned for this model: step 18 (21% less spatial
sampling than the old step-16 default) is what knowledge/24-8-report.md's frame-level
test (§13) actually measured convnext_tiny at -- it beats convnext_pico@16 on that
test despite the coarser sampling. 23.0 fps is the standing deployment target for the
whole Aug26_78K campaign (5090, GPU_SCALE 1.6x over the A6000 bench).
2026-08-25 UPDATE: model switched from mix_convnext_tiny (legacy forth_altinay
protocol, pre-Aug26_78K) to fzcnxtiny_convnext_tiny (Aug26_78K, 4ch+DoLP, 10-class,
coverage carve-out -- knowledge/24-8-report.md §7/§8/§13/§14). This is the
'challenger' the report's own §15 does NOT declare a clean ship call for: coverage
and the frame-level test both favor it (+4.34 TIER_A coverage at n=3, ESTABLISHED;
wins the matched-Hz frame-level comparison 96.40 vs 95.95), but the factory-KPI ship
rule is UNRESOLVED at n=3 for this model -- numerically a hair worse than the
incumbent, inside noise. §15: 'the data supports switching to convnext_tiny@step18 on
every generalization measure this campaign has; it does not support a claim that the
factory KPI has improved.' This file now reflects a decision to ship on the
generalization evidence anyway -- see §15 before reverting or re-litigating that call.
The lightweight mix_shufflenet_v2_x1_0 alternate preset was removed here: it has no
equivalent run under the current protocol, and leaving its legacy numbers next to
freshly recalibrated ones would misrepresent it as current.
PUBLISHING NOTE, verified 2026-08-25: fzcnxtiny_convnext_tiny_20260819_161921.zip IS
already live at http://ammar.gr/magician/models/CameraV2Models/ (uploadModels.sh runs
with ALLOW_ALL=1 hardcoded, so the allowlist in scripts/upload_allowlist.txt does not
actually gate what reaches the server -- it is commented out there, but that file is
currently informational only, not enforced). Ran the exact startup path end to end
against a clean directory standing in for a deployment box: ensure_model() fetched
and extracted the newest archive, ClassifierPnm loaded it with zero missing/unexpected
state-dict keys, and applying this file's 'default' preset produced the same 77.3%
detected / 0.79% false-alarm gate the threshold_reference below states. Auto-download
and use are both confirmed working, not just configured.

_comment: Measured operating curve for the default model, so an operator can pick a gate
level without opening the curve file. Read verbatim from
Aug26_78K factory-val split, seed 42, 2 epochs, monitored-best checkpoint.
detected = fraction of DEFECT tiles flagged. false_alarm = fraction of CLEAN tiles
flagged; multiply by the tiles-per-frame count to get crosses per frame.
This curve is an AGGREGATE, incidence-weighted number over the factory val split
(87.6% welding) -- knowledge/24-8-report.md §2.5 argues this instrument is weak for
exactly the class-balance reasons that make convnext_tiny's gain hard to see here.
The per-class TIER_A coverage case (+4.34, ESTABLISHED, §14) is the stronger evidence
for this model; this curve exists only to calibrate a deployable gate threshold.
A false-alarm rate below ~0.24% is NOT reachable: the sweep bottoms out at threshold

configurations.name: default
configurations.description: fzcnxtiny_convnext_tiny (Aug26_78K challenger, step 18) at ~0.8% false alarms on the factory-val curve. Best per-class coverage in the campaign (+4.34 TIER_A, ESTABLISHED n=3, knowledge/24-8-report.md §14) -- see the file-level README before treating this as a fully settled ship decision.

configurations.name: low_false_alarm
configurations.description: Same model near the trainer's deployment point (~0.5% false-alarm budget). Roughly halves false alarms relative to default for 4 points of factory-curve detection.

configurations.name: minimal_false_alarm
configurations.description: Strictest useful gate: 0.24% false alarms on the factory curve. Use when crosses are acted on automatically and a false stop is expensive. Below roughly 0.24% FA is not reachable on this model.

configurations.name: one_percent_fa
configurations.description: Highest detection available inside a 1% false-alarm budget on the factory curve.

configurations.name: high_recall
configurations.description: fzcnxtiny_convnext_tiny at its trainer-calibrated KPI-optimal gate. Use only where an operator reviews the crosses -- the false-alarm rate is an order of magnitude higher than the default.
